meta.source: workspace-mcp 2.2.1 tools/list (MIT, taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp), captured offline with no network
meta.args: --transport streamable-http --permissions gmail:readonly+drafts+send drive:full docs:full sheets:full --tool-tier extended

tools.name: copy_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a copy of an existing Google Drive file.

This tool copies the template document to a new location with an optional new name.
The copy maintains all formatting and content from the original file.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to copy. Required.

new_name.description: New name for the copied file. If not provided, uses "Copy of [original name]".

parent_folder_id.description: The ID of the folder where the copy should be created. Defaults to 'root' (My Drive).

copy_comments.description: Copy open comments and suggestions (Docs/Sheets/Slides only). Defaults to False.

tools.name: create_doc
tools.description:
Creates a new Google Doc and optionally inserts initial content.

`content` is inserted as plain text (Markdown is not rendered); use
import_to_google_doc to create a doc from Markdown.

After creation, the document body starts at index 1. A new empty doc
has total length 2 (one section break at index 0, one newline at index 1).

To build a rich document after creation, use batch_update_doc with
insert_text operations using end_of_segment=true to append content
sequentially without calculating indices. Then call inspect_doc_structure
to get exact positions before applying formatting in a separate batch call.

content.description: Optional initial plain text content to insert

folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared
drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

tools.name: create_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a new file in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.
Accepts direct text content, inline base64 bytes, or a fileUrl to fetch content from.
Where local file access is disabled it can instead return an upload URL for the
caller to PUT file bytes to.
This stores the supplied bytes without converting them to Google Docs, Sheets, or
Slides. Use the matching import_to_google_* tool for Google-native conversion.

file_name.description: The name for the new file.

content.description: If provided, the content to write to the file.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

mime_type.description: The MIME type of the file. Defaults to 'text/plain'; required with return_upload_url.

fileUrl.description: If provided, fetches the file content from this URL. Supports http:// and https://; file:// only where local file access is enabled. Where it is disabled, files on the caller's machine go through an upload URL instead (see the upload-URL parameter, if offered).

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

return_upload_url.description: Return a Google resumable-upload session URL for a new file of mime_type instead of creating it from inline content; the caller PUTs the bytes there directly (no Authorization header). Preferred for large or binary files. Not combinable with other content sources. Offered only where local file access is disabled.

tools.name: create_drive_folder
tools.description: Creates a new folder in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.

folder_name.description: The name for the new folder.

parent_folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.
For shared drives, use a folder ID within that shared drive.

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Creates a new Google Spreadsheet.

title.description: The title of the new spreadsheet. Required.

sheet_names.description: List of sheet names to create. If not provided, creates one sheet with default name.

folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared
drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

tools.name: draft_gmail_message
tools.description:
Creates a draft email in the user's Gmail account. Supports new, reply, and forward
drafts with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to draft from
configured alias addresses.

To save a forward as a draft for review, pass forward_message_id. The original
subject, body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are
carried over. In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note, subject is
optional, and threading, reply, and signature options do not apply.

SCHEDULED SEND IS NOT AVAILABLE. Gmail's REST API exposes no send-time
parameter; the Schedule send feature is web-UI only, and a message cannot be
placed in the Scheduled folder through the API. Do not claim a message was
scheduled. To deliver at a chosen time, create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message then, or call
users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule the draft in the Gmail UI.

subject.description: Email subject. Required for a new draft. Optional when replying with thread_id (inherits the parent message's subject, adding 'Re:' only if absent) or when forwarding (then defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body. Required unless forwarding, where it becomes an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Email body format. Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content. With 'html', write real markup; an entity-escaped body ('<div>') is rejected.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to save a forward of that message as a draft for review. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the account's default Send As address, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail returns no usable Send-As entry or settings access is not authorized.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: 'url' (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR 'path' (file path, auto-encodes), OR 'content' (standard base64, not urlsafe) + 'filename'. Optional 'mime_type'. Optional 'content_id' (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment.

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

direction.description: Base text direction of the body. 'auto' (default) takes it from the first strong character (a right-to-left script gives 'rtl', anything else 'ltr'); 'ltr'/'rtl' force it. On a forward it orients the note.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.

tools.name: export_doc_to_pdf
tools.description: Exports a Google Doc to PDF format and saves it to Google Drive.

document_id.description: ID of the Google Doc to export

pdf_filename.description: Name for the PDF file (optional - if not provided, uses original name + "_PDF")

folder_id.description: Drive folder ID to save PDF in (optional - if not provided, saves in root)

tools.name: find_and_replace_doc
tools.description:
Finds and replaces text throughout a Google Doc. No index calculation required.

This is the safest way to update specific text in a document because it
does not require knowing any indices. Use this tool when you need to:
- Replace placeholder text (e.g., {{TITLE}}) with real content
- Update specific words or phrases throughout the document
- Make targeted text changes without risk of index errors

For building documents from scratch, consider inserting text with unique
placeholders via batch_update_doc, then using this tool to replace them.

document_id.description: ID of the document to update

tab_id.description: Optional ID of the tab to target

tools.name: format_sheet_range
tools.description:
Applies formatting to a range: colors, number formats, text wrapping,
alignment, text styling, cell merging/unmerging, borders, and dropdown lists.

Colors accept hex strings (#RRGGBB). Number formats follow Sheets types
(e.g., NUMBER, CURRENCY, DATE, PERCENT). If no sheet name is provided,
the first sheet is used.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

range_name.description: A1-style range (optionally with sheet name). Required.

number_format_pattern.description: Custom pattern for the number format.

wrap_strategy.description:
Text wrap strategy - WRAP (wrap text within
cell), CLIP (clip text at cell boundary), or OVERFLOW_CELL (allow text
to overflow into adjacent empty cells).

horizontal_alignment.description:
Horizontal text alignment - LEFT,
CENTER, or RIGHT.

vertical_alignment.description:
Vertical text alignment - TOP, MIDDLE,
or BOTTOM.

merge_cells.description:
True merges the range, False unmerges it.
Merging keeps only the top-left value of each merged group.

merge_type.description:
MERGE_ALL (default), MERGE_COLUMNS, or
MERGE_ROWS. Setting it implies merge_cells=True.

borders.description:
Which borders to draw, comma-separated: all,
outer, inner, top, bottom, left, right, inner_horizontal,
inner_vertical (e.g., "outer" or "bottom,inner_horizontal").
"none" removes every border in the range.

border_style.description:
SOLID (default), SOLID_MEDIUM, SOLID_THICK,
DASHED, DOTTED, or DOUBLE. Requires borders.

border_color.description:
Hex border color (default black). Requires
borders.

dropdown_values.description:
Turns every cell in the range into
a dropdown offering these values (e.g., ["open", "done"]).

dropdown_strict.description:
With dropdown_values: reject other
input (default True) or only show a warning (False).

clear_dropdown.description:
Remove all data validation from the
range: dropdowns, but also checkboxes and other validation rules.

tools.name: get_doc_as_markdown
tools.description:
Reads a Google Doc and returns it as clean Markdown with optional comment context.

Unlike get_doc_content which returns plain text, this tool preserves document
formatting as Markdown: headings, bold/italic/strikethrough, links, code spans,
ordered/unordered lists with nesting, and tables.

When comments are included (the default), each comment's anchor text — the specific
text the comment was attached to — is preserved, giving full context for the discussion.

document_id.description:
ID of the Google Doc (or full URL). When a full URL is provided
and it contains a ?tab= query parameter, that tab is used automatically
unless tab_id is also specified (explicit tab_id takes precedence).

comment_mode.description:
How to display comments:
- "inline": Footnote-style references placed at the anchor text location (default)
- "appendix": All comments grouped at the bottom with blockquoted anchor text
- "none": No comments included

include_resolved.description: Whether to include resolved comments (default: False)

suggestions_view_mode.description:
How to render suggestions in the returned content:
- "DEFAULT_FOR_CURRENT_ACCESS": Default based on user's access level
- "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE": Suggested changes appear inline in the document
- "PREVIEW_SUGGESTIONS_ACCEPTED": Preview as if all suggestions were accepted
- "PREVIEW_WITHOUT_SUGGESTIONS": Preview as if all suggestions were rejected

tab_id.description:
Optional ID of a single tab to read (from inspect_doc_structure).
When given, only that tab's content is rendered, without its child tabs
and without a tab heading, and comments are listed as document-wide.
When omitted, every tab is rendered. Pass "" to read every tab of a
URL that carries ?tab=. This filters output only: the whole document
is still fetched.

include_colors.description:
Follow text that has an explicit RGB foreground color
with "[color: #rrggbb]" (default: False). Theme colors are not shown.

tools.name: get_doc_content
tools.description:
Retrieves content of a Google Doc or a Drive file (like .docx) identified by document_id.
- Native Google Docs: Fetches content via Docs API.
- Office files (.docx, etc.) stored in Drive: Downloads via Drive API and extracts text.

By default, native Google Docs text is index-aligned with the document:
empty paragraphs are preserved and every non-text element that occupies an
index (inline object, page break, footnote reference, ...) is rendered as one
U+FFFC placeholder per index. The document body starts at index 1, so an
offset n into the text that follows "--- CONTENT ---" is document index n + 1,
and that index can be passed straight to format_text or delete_text. Tables
and multi-tab documents interleave separators, so alignment holds up to the
first table or tab header.

Set preserve_context=True for readable link destinations, internal targets,
smart-chip values, table boundaries, headers, footers, footnotes, and object
context exposed by the Docs API. This output is plain text, not Markdown,
and its offsets must not be used as document editing indices. Comments,
revision history, exact visual layout, and chip details hidden by the API
are not included. Use get_doc_as_markdown for formatting or comments.

document_id.description:
ID of the Google Doc or Drive file (or full URL). A Docs
URL's ?tab= selects that tab unless tab_id is also specified.

suggestions_view_mode.description:
How to render suggestions in the returned content:
- "DEFAULT_FOR_CURRENT_ACCESS": Default based on user's access level
- "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE": Suggested changes appear inline in the document
- "PREVIEW_SUGGESTIONS_ACCEPTED": Preview as if all suggestions were accepted
- "PREVIEW_WITHOUT_SUGGESTIONS": Preview as if all suggestions were rejected

tab_id.description:
Optional ID of a single tab to read (from inspect_doc_structure).
When given, only that tab's content is returned with no tab separator,
so the default output stays index-aligned with that tab. When
omitted, every tab is returned with "--- TAB: ... ---" markers.
Pass "" to read every tab of a URL that carries ?tab=. This
filters output only: the whole document is still fetched.

preserve_context.description:
Include readable semantic annotations for native Docs.
Defaults to False to retain index alignment. Office extraction is
unaffected. With tab_id, only the selected tab is rendered.

tools.name: get_drive_file_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of a specific Google Drive file by ID, supporting files in shared drives.

• Native Google Docs, Sheets, Slides → exported as text / CSV.
• Office files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) → unzipped & parsed with std-lib to
  extract readable text.
• PDFs → text extracted with pypdf when possible; scanned/image-only PDFs
  fall back to a download hint.
• Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) → returned as MCP image content after the
  metadata header. SVG → returned as its markup; raster images it embeds
  as base64 are attached as image content, numbered to match their place
  in the markup. BMP and TIFF → still returned as base64 text.
• Any other file → downloaded; tries UTF-8 decode, else notes binary.

tools.name: get_drive_file_download_url
tools.description:
Downloads a Google Drive file and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
In stateless mode (no file storage), returns the file itself as an embedded
resource, up to WORKSPACE_MCP_STATELESS_INLINE_MAX_BYTES (default 10 MiB,
and never more than WORKSPACE_MCP_MAX_FILE_BYTES when that is set).

For Google native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides), exports to a useful format:
- Google Docs -> PDF (default) or DOCX if export_format='docx'
- Google Sheets -> XLSX (default), PDF if export_format='pdf', or CSV if export_format='csv'
- Google Slides -> PDF (default) or PPTX if export_format='pptx'

For other files, downloads the original file format.

file_id.description: The Google Drive file ID to download.

export_format.description:
Optional export format for Google native files.
          Options: 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'pptx'.
          If not specified, uses sensible defaults (PDF for Docs/Slides, XLSX for Sheets).
          For Sheets: supports 'csv', 'pdf', or 'xlsx' (default).

tools.name: get_drive_shareable_link
tools.description: Gets the shareable link for a Google Drive file or folder.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder to get the shareable link for. Required.

tools.name: get_gmail_attachment_content
tools.description:
Downloads an email attachment and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
May re-fetch message metadata to resolve filename and MIME type.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

return_base64.description:
When True, includes the full attachment as a
standard base64 string in the response (in addition to any file
path or download URL). Useful for sandboxed clients that cannot
reach localhost download URLs or the MCP server's local file
paths (e.g. containerized agents with network allowlists). The
returned base64 uses the standard alphabet, so it can be passed
directly to tools like ``draft_gmail_message`` that expect
standard (not URL-safe) base64. Default False preserves the
existing behavior and response size.

attachment_index.description:
Zero-based attachment position from
the message-content response. Lets the server resolve Gmail's
refreshed attachment IDs against current metadata before every
download, selecting the current attachment ID, filename and MIME type.

tools.name: get_gmail_message_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the full content (subject, sender, recipients, body) of a specific Gmail message.

Bodies are returned inline and truncated at 20,000 characters. Set full=True to
get the complete, untruncated message instead: it is exported to storage and the
response carries a short-lived download URL (HTTP transport) or file path (stdio
transport) rather than the body, so large messages never stream through the model
context. Stateless deployments without GCS staging have no storage, so there
full=True returns the untruncated body inline; with GCS staging configured it
returns a signed download URL like any other HTTP deployment.

message_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail message to retrieve.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

full.description: When True, return the COMPLETE untruncated message: saved to storage and referenced by download URL/file path instead of the body text. In stateless mode without GCS staging, the body is returned inline; with GCS staging, a signed download URL is returned. Use for messages large enough to hit the truncation limit, or when byte-exact fidelity is needed (pair with body_format='raw' for a .eml export).

format.description:
Message format. "full" (default) includes
the body and attachments, "metadata" only headers.

include_headers.description:
When False, omit the Subject/From/To/Date header
summary (attached messages' too), and with full=True name the export
after the message ID. Requires format='full'; body_format='raw' is only
allowed when the raw message is exported to a file.

include_links.description: When True, append a LINKS section listing the http(s) URLs from the HTML body that the text output omits. Only applies to body_format='text'.

tools.name: get_gmail_messages_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 messages per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

message_ids.description: List of Gmail message IDs to retrieve; fetched in batches of 25.

format.description: Message format. "full" includes body, "metadata" only headers.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

include_links.description: When True, append a LINKS section listing the http(s) URLs from the HTML body that the text output omits. Only applies to body_format='text'.

tools.name: get_gmail_thread_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the complete content of a Gmail conversation thread, including all messages.

Optionally also returns structured ownership analysis so a caller can
determine who sent the last message and who owes whom a response without
re-parsing the formatted string or making a second tool call.

thread_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail thread to retrieve.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

include_analysis.description: When True, the return value is a dict with both the formatted thread content AND structured ownership analysis (last sender, ball-in-court verdict, per-sender message counts, participants). Defaults to False, in which case the existing string return shape is preserved.

include_links.description: When True, append a LINKS section listing the http(s) URLs from the HTML body that the text output omits. Only applies to body_format='text'.

tools.name: get_spreadsheet_info
tools.description: Gets information about a specific spreadsheet including its sheets.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet to get info for. Required.

tools.name: import_to_google_doc
tools.description:
Imports a file (Markdown, DOCX, TXT, HTML, RTF, ODT) into Google Docs format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source file to native Google Docs format,
preserving formatting like headings, lists, bold, italic, etc.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Doc; the extension is dropped from the title. Without 'source_format', its extension also sets the format of 'content' or 'base64_content' (e.g. 'Notes.md' so Markdown tables are not imported as plain text).

content.description: Text content for text-based formats. Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the file from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('md', 'markdown', 'docx', 'txt', 'html', 'rtf', 'odt').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a binary source such as DOCX or ODT.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

return_upload_url.description: Return a Google resumable-upload session URL instead of ingesting the source here; the caller PUTs the source bytes there directly (no Authorization header) and Drive converts them. Requires source_format; not combinable with other content sources. Offered only where local file access is disabled.

tools.name: import_to_google_sheets
tools.description:
Imports a spreadsheet (XLSX, XLS, ODS, CSV, TSV) into Google Sheets format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source spreadsheet to native Google Sheets format,
preserving rows, columns, sheets, and values.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Sheets spreadsheet; the extension is dropped from the title. Without 'source_format', its extension also sets the format of 'content' or 'base64_content' (e.g. 'Data.csv').

content.description: Text content for text-based formats (CSV, TSV). Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the spreadsheet from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('xlsx', 'xls', 'ods', 'csv', 'tsv').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for an XLSX, XLS, or ODS source.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

return_upload_url.description: Return a Google resumable-upload session URL instead of ingesting the source here; the caller PUTs the source bytes there directly (no Authorization header) and Drive converts them. Requires source_format; not combinable with other content sources. Offered only where local file access is disabled.

tools.name: import_to_google_slides
tools.description:
Imports a presentation (PPTX, PPT, ODP) into Google Slides format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source presentation to native Google Slides format,
preserving slides, layouts, text, and images.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Slides presentation; the extension is dropped from the title. Without 'source_format', its extension also sets the format of 'base64_content' (e.g. 'Deck.pptx').

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the presentation from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('pptx', 'ppt', 'odp').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a PPTX or ODP source.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

return_upload_url.description: Return a Google resumable-upload session URL instead of ingesting the source here; the caller PUTs the source bytes there directly (no Authorization header) and Drive converts them. Requires source_format; not combinable with other content sources. Offered only where local file access is disabled.

tools.name: insert_doc_elements
tools.description: Inserts structural elements like tables, lists, or page breaks into a Google Doc.

document_id.description: ID of the document to update

rows.description: Number of rows for table (required for table)

columns.description: Number of columns for table (required for table)

text.description: Initial text content for list items

tools.name: list_docs_in_folder
tools.description: Lists Google Docs within a specific Drive folder.

folder_id.description: ID of the Drive folder to list. Defaults to 'root'.

page_size.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Defaults to 100.

page_token.description:
Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to
retrieve the next page of results.

tools.name: list_document_comments
tools.description: List all comments from a Google Document (optional max_comments to limit results).

tools.name: list_drive_items
tools.description:
Lists files/folders or shared drive containers, supporting shared drives.
If `drive_id` is specified, lists items within that shared drive. `folder_id` is then relative to that drive (or use drive_id as folder_id for root).
If `drive_id` is not specified, lists items from user's "My Drive" and accessible shared drives (if `include_items_from_all_drives` is True).
Set `resource_type` to "shared_drives" to list shared drive containers instead of folder contents.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Google Drive folder. Defaults to 'root'. For a shared drive, this can be the shared drive's ID to list its root, or a folder ID within that shared drive.

page_size.description: The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive. If provided, the listing is scoped to this drive.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether items from all accessible shared drives should be included if `drive_id` is not set. Defaults to True.

corpora.description: Corpus to query ('user', 'drive', 'allDrives'). If `drive_id` is set and `corpora` is None, 'drive' is used. If None and no `drive_id`, 'allDrives' is used when `include_items_from_all_drives` is True.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

resource_type.description:
What to list. Use "items" for folder contents or
                 "shared_drives" for shared drive containers. Defaults to "items".

query.description:
Shared drive query used only when resource_type="shared_drives",
                   e.g. "name contains 'Engineering'".

include_organizers.description:
When resource_type="shared_drives", include principals
                       with the organizer role. This costs one extra permissions.list
                       API call per shared drive returned. Defaults to False.

tools.name: list_gmail_labels
tools.description: Lists labels in the user's Gmail account.

prefix.description:
Return only labels whose name starts with this
exact (case-sensitive) string. users.labels.list accepts no filter,
so the full list is fetched and narrowed here: this shrinks what the
caller receives, not the API call.

include_system.description:
Include Gmail system labels (INBOX, SENT, ...).
Set False to return user labels only.

tools.name: list_sheet_tables
tools.description:
Lists all structured tables in a spreadsheet with their IDs, names, ranges,
and column details. Use this to find table IDs for append_table_rows.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

tools.name: list_spreadsheets
tools.description: Lists spreadsheets from Google Drive that the user has access to.

max_results.description: Maximum number of spreadsheets to return. Defaults to 25.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

corpora.description:
Corpus to search ('user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
Defaults to 'drive' when drive_id is set, otherwise 'allDrives'.

tools.name: manage_document_comment
tools.description: Manage comments on a Google Document.

tools.name: manage_drive_access
tools.description:
Consolidated tool for managing Google Drive file and folder access permissions.

Supports granting, batch-granting, updating, revoking permissions, and
transferring file ownership -- all through a single entry point.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

action.description:
The access management action to perform. Required. One of:
- "grant": Share with a single user, group, domain, or anyone.
- "grant_batch": Share with multiple recipients in one call.
- "update": Modify an existing permission (role or expiration).
- "revoke": Remove an existing permission.
- "transfer_owner": Transfer file ownership to another user.

share_with.description:
Email address (user/group), domain name (domain),
or omit for 'anyone'. Used by "grant".

role.description:
Permission role -- 'reader', 'commenter', or 'writer'.
Used by "grant" (defaults to 'reader') and "update".

share_type.description:
Type of sharing -- 'user', 'group', 'domain', or 'anyone'.
Used by "grant". Defaults to 'user'.

permission_id.description:
The permission ID to modify or remove.
Required for "update" and "revoke" actions.

recipients.description:
List of recipient objects for
"grant_batch". Each should have: email (str), role (str, optional),
share_type (str, optional), expiration_time (str, optional). For domain
shares use 'domain' field instead of 'email'.

send_notification.description:
Whether to send notification emails. Defaults to True.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

email_message.description:
Custom notification email message.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

expiration_time.description:
Expiration in RFC 3339 format
(e.g., "2025-01-15T00:00:00Z"). Used by "grant" and "update".

allow_file_discovery.description:
For 'domain'/'anyone' shares, whether
the file appears in search. Used by "grant".

new_owner_email.description:
Email of the new owner.
Required for "transfer_owner".

move_to_new_owners_root.description:
Move file to the new owner's My Drive root.
Defaults to False. Used by "transfer_owner".

tools.name: modify_doc_text
tools.description:
Modifies text in a Google Doc - can insert/replace text and/or apply formatting in a single operation.

TIP: To append text to the end of the document without calculating indices,
set end_of_segment=true. This avoids index calculation errors.

HEADING MODE: Pass heading instead of start_index to edit the body below a
heading, up to the next heading of equal or shallower level. text is
rendered as Markdown and replaces that body; end_of_segment=true appends
instead. Formatting parameters without text format the whole body.

For ordinary header/footer text, prefer update_doc_headers_footers.
Only pass segment_id when you already have a real header/footer/footnote
segment ID from inspect_doc_structure output. Do not guess IDs such as
"kix.header" or "kix.footer".

document_id.description: ID of the document to update

start_index.description:
Start position for operation using Docs API indices from
inspect_doc_structure. For the main body, 0 is also accepted as an
alias for the first writable position. Required unless heading is set.

end_index.description: End position for text replacement/formatting (if not provided with text, text is inserted)

text.description:
New text to insert or replace with (optional - can format existing text without changing it).
Rendered as Markdown when heading is set.

heading.description:
Text of a body heading (case-insensitive, must match exactly one) whose
section to edit instead of start_index/end_index

heading_level.description: Optional 1-6 heading level to narrow the heading match

tab_id.description: Optional document tab ID to target (required with heading when the doc has multiple tabs)

segment_id.description: Optional header/footer/footnote segment ID to target

end_of_segment.description: Insert text at the end of the targeted segment instead of start_index

bold.description: Whether to make text bold (True/False/None to leave unchanged)

italic.description: Whether to make text italic (True/False/None to leave unchanged)

underline.description: Whether to underline text (True/False/None to leave unchanged)

strikethrough.description: Whether to strike through text (True/False/None to leave unchanged)

font_weight.description: Font weight (100-900 in steps of 100; requires font_family)

clear_link.description: Remove hyperlink from the target range

tools.name: modify_sheet_values
tools.description:
Modifies values in a specific range of a Google Sheet - can write, update, or clear values,
or insert Smart Chips (Drive files/folders or People).

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

values.description: 2D array of values to write/update. Can be a JSON string or Python list. Required unless clear_values=True or chips is provided.

value_input_option.description: How to interpret input values ("RAW" or "USER_ENTERED"). Defaults to "USER_ENTERED".

clear_values.description: If True, clears the range instead of writing values. Defaults to False.

chips.description:
Smart chip(s) to insert instead of values:
- A single URL or email string for a single cell (e.g., "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/123", "user@example.com").
- A list of URLs or emails for a single cell (multiple chips) or across cells (e.g., ["https://...", "https://..."]).
- A 2D list of URLs/emails matching a grid range. For a single-row or single-column
  range, each inner list is instead the chips for one cell (e.g., [["a@x.com", "b@x.com"]]
  puts both chips in the first cell of "A1:C1").
- A dict or list of dicts with explicit properties (e.g., {"type": "drive", "uri": "..."}, {"type": "person", "email": "..."}).
- A JSON-encoded string representing any of the above formats.

chip_type.description: Explicit chip type if passing raw strings in chips: "drive" (default for URLs/IDs) or "person" (default for emails).

tools.name: read_sheet_values
tools.description: Reads values from a specific range in a Google Sheet.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

range_name.description:
The range to read (e.g., "Sheet1!A1:D10", "A1:D10").
Defaults to "A1:Z1000". Open-ended or oversized ranges are clamped to
at most 1000 rows before the Sheets API request to bound memory use.

include_hyperlinks.description:
If True, also fetch hyperlink metadata for the range.
Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

include_notes.description:
If True, also fetch cell notes for the range.
Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

include_formulas.description:
If True, also fetch raw formula strings for cells that
contain formulas. Useful for identifying cross-sheet references before writing
back to a range. Defaults to False to avoid an extra API request.

include_smart_chips.description:
If True, also fetch smart chips metadata (Drive files/folders
and People chips) for the range. Defaults to False to avoid expensive includeGridData requests.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Searches for Google Docs by name using Drive API (mimeType filter).

query.description: Text to search for in document names.

page_size.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description:
Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to
retrieve the next page of results.

corpora.description:
Corpus to search ('user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
Defaults to 'drive' when drive_id is set, otherwise 'allDrives'.

drive_id.description: Optional shared drive ID to search.

tools.name: search_drive_files
tools.description: Searches for files and folders within a user's Google Drive, including shared drives.

query.description:
The search query string. Supports Google Drive search operators.
         NOTE: Owner-based queries ('user@example.com' in owners) DO NOT WORK in Shared Drives
         because files are owned by the shared drive itself, not individual users.
         For recent files by a specific user in Shared Drives, search by modifiedTime
         and use order_by='modifiedTime desc' instead.

page_size.description: The maximum number of files to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive to search. If None, behavior depends on `corpora` and `include_items_from_all_drives`.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether shared drive items should be included in results. Defaults to True. This is effective when not specifying a `drive_id`.

corpora.description:
Bodies of items to query (e.g., 'user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
                     If 'drive_id' is specified and 'corpora' is None, it defaults to 'drive'.
                     Otherwise it defaults to 'allDrives' when `include_items_from_all_drives` is True.
                     Pass 'user' to search only My Drive and files shared with the user.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

include_trashed.description:
Whether to include files in the trash. Defaults to False, matching
                    the Drive web UI and `list_drive_items`. Ignored when `query` already
                    contains its own `trashed` clause (`=` or `!=`), which always wins.

tools.name: search_gmail_messages
tools.description:
Searches messages in a user's Gmail account based on a query.
Returns both Message IDs and Thread IDs for each found message, along with Gmail web interface links for manual verification.
Supports pagination via page_token parameter.

query.description:
The search query. Supports standard Gmail search operators.
Results include drafts unless the query excludes them (e.g. in:sent or -in:drafts).

page_size.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the next_page_token from a previous response.

include_headers.description:
If True, also fetch each message's metadata and include
Subject, From, Date and label IDs (e.g. DRAFT, SENT) per result. Costs one
metadata get per result, grouped into HTTP batches of up to 10, plus retries
for transient failures.
Defaults to False (output unchanged from prior versions).

tools.name: send_gmail_message
tools.description:
Sends an email using the user's Gmail account. Supports new emails, replies, and
forwards, with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to send
from configured alias addresses.

To forward an existing message, pass forward_message_id. The original subject,
body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are carried over.
In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note and subject is optional.
Threading, reply, and signature options do not apply when forwarding.

THIS TOOL SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT SCHEDULE. Gmail's REST API exposes no
send-time parameter; Schedule send is a web-UI feature with no API equivalent,
so no argument to this tool can defer delivery. Never tell a user a message
was scheduled. For "prepare now, deliver later", create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message at the chosen time, or
call users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule that draft in the Gmail UI.

to.description: Recipient email address. Optional when replying with reply_all=True, which derives it from the thread.

subject.description: Email subject. Required for a new message. Optional when replying with thread_id (inherits the parent message's subject, adding 'Re:' only if absent) or when forwarding (defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML). Required when sending. When forwarding, this is an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Format of the body content (and of the prepended note when forwarding). Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content. With 'html', write real markup; an entity-escaped body ('<div>') is rejected.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to forward that message instead of composing a new one. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the authenticated user's email.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

direction.description: Base text direction of the body. 'auto' (default) takes it from the first strong character (a right-to-left script gives 'rtl', anything else 'ltr'); 'ltr'/'rtl' force it. On a forward it orients the note.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the message being replied to as a quoted original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.

tools.name: set_drive_file_permissions
tools.description:
Sets file-level sharing settings and controls link sharing for a Google Drive file or folder.

This is a high-level tool for the most common permission changes. Use this to toggle
"anyone with the link" access or configure file-level sharing behavior. For managing
individual user/group permissions, use share_drive_file or update_drive_permission instead.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

link_sharing.description:
Control "anyone with the link" access for the file.
- "off": Disable "anyone with the link" access for this file.
- "reader": Anyone with the link can view.
- "commenter": Anyone with the link can comment.
- "writer": Anyone with the link can edit.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can change permissions and share.
If False, only the owner can share. Defaults to None (no change).

copy_requires_writer_permission.description:
Whether viewers and commenters
are prevented from copying, printing, or downloading. Defaults to None (no change).

tools.name: update_drive_file
tools.description:
Updates metadata, properties, and/or content of a Google Drive file.

Providing new content (inline as ``content``, fetched from ``file_url``, or on a
local server read from a file path) replaces the file's content in place,
preserving the existing file ID, sharing, comments, and links.
For native Google Docs/Sheets/Slides the source is uploaded with its source MIME
type so the Drive API applies the same format conversion as import_to_google_doc
(markdown headings, tables, bold, etc.). For any other file (.md, .txt, .pdf, ...)
there is nothing to convert, so the bytes are written back as-is under the file's
own MIME type. Metadata and content can be updated in a single call.

``mode='append'``/``'prepend'`` splice ``content`` onto the file's existing text
server-side, so only the new text has to be supplied — no need to send the whole
file back to rewrite it.

Drive shortcuts are handled according to the kind of update: supported
resource-local metadata changes (rename, move, trash, star, description, and
custom properties) apply to the supplied shortcut, while content replacement
follows the shortcut and updates its target. To avoid applying metadata to the
wrong resource, a shortcut call cannot combine content with resource-local
metadata. Update the shortcut metadata and target content in separate calls.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to update. Required.

mime_type.description:
New MIME type (note: changing type may require
content upload). For a shortcut ID, this must accompany content and applies
to the resolved target.

add_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to add as parents.

remove_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to remove from parents.

trashed.description: Whether to move file to/from trash.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can share the file. Pass the
target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a shortcut resource.

copy_requires_writer_permission.description:
Whether copying requires writer
permission. Pass the target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a
shortcut resource.

properties.description: Custom key-value properties for the file.

content.description: New text content for text-based formats (markdown, TXT, HTML).

file_url.description: Remote http(s) URL to fetch new content from.

source_format.description:
Source format hint for conversion
(md, markdown, docx, txt, html, rtf, odt). Auto-detected when omitted, and
ignored for non-Google files, which are uploaded without conversion.
Provide at most one content source.

mode.description:
How to apply the new content — 'replace' (default), 'append', or
'prepend'. Append/prepend require 'content' and a UTF-8 text file such as
.md or .txt; a newline is inserted at the seam if neither side has one.
For native Google Docs use insert_doc_elements, modify_doc_text, or
find_and_replace_doc, which edit in place instead of rewriting the file.

return_upload_url.description:
Return a Google resumable-upload session URL to
PUT the replacement bytes to directly (no Authorization header); any
metadata changes take effect with the upload. Only with
mode='replace'; not combinable with another content source. Here
mime_type names the MIME type of the bytes to be uploaded; on a native
Google file it is required, names only that, and leaves the file's type
untouched. Offered only where local file access is disabled.

tools.name: update_paragraph_style
tools.description:
Apply paragraph-level formatting, heading styles, and/or list formatting to a range in a Google Doc.

This tool can apply named heading styles (H1-H6) for semantic document structure,
create bulleted or numbered lists with nested indentation, and customize paragraph
properties like alignment, spacing, and indentation. All operations can be applied
in a single call.

start_index.description:
Start position using Docs API indices from
inspect_doc_structure. For the main body, 0 is also accepted as an
alias for the first writable position.

end_index.description: End position (exclusive) - should cover the entire paragraph

heading_level.description:
Heading level 0-6 (0 = NORMAL_TEXT, 1 = H1, 2 = H2, etc.)
           Use for semantic document structure

indent_first_line.description: First line indent in points (e.g., 36 for 0.5 inch)

space_above.description: Space above paragraph in points (e.g., 12 for one line)

named_style_type.description:
Direct named style type - 'NORMAL_TEXT', 'TITLE', 'SUBTITLE',
             'HEADING_1' through 'HEADING_6'. Mutually exclusive with heading_level.

tab_id.description: Optional document tab ID to target

segment_id.description: Optional header/footer/footnote segment ID to target

keep_lines_together.description: Keep all lines of the paragraph together

keep_with_next.description: Keep the paragraph with the next paragraph

page_break_before.description: Start the paragraph on a new page

border_edges.description:
Paragraph border edges to update ('top', 'bottom', 'left',
          'right', or 'between'); omit to update all four outer edges

border_dash.description: Border dash style ('SOLID', 'DOT', or 'DASH'; defaults to 'SOLID')

list_type.description: Create a list from existing paragraphs ('UNORDERED' for bullets, 'ORDERED' for numbers, 'CHECKBOX' for checklists), or 'NONE' to remove existing list formatting from the range. Use 'NONE' when text inserted after a list has inherited its bullets: setting named_style_type or heading_level does not clear list membership, only 'NONE' does.

list_nesting_level.description:
Nesting level for lists (0-8, where 0 is top level, default is 0)
               Use higher levels for nested/indented list items

bullet_preset.description: Optional explicit Google Docs bullet preset
